author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing shows the first page for a page value below 1
summary: Opening the owner listing with a page value below 1 shows the first page as a normal response (HTTP 200) instead of the error page, with or without a last-name search.
acceptance_criteria: given a request to /owners with page=0, when the owner listing is opened, then the response is HTTP 200 and the first page of owners is listed, with no error page
given a negative page value, including the lowest whole number the listing can read, when the owner listing is opened, then the response is HTTP 200 and the first page of owners is listed
given a page value below 1, when the owner listing is shown, then the first page is the one marked as current and the page controls act from it
given a last name matching more than one owner and a page value below 1, when the search runs, then the first page of matches is listed
given a page value below 1, when a search matches one owner, then that owner's record still opens directly
given a page value below 1, when a search matches no owner, then the search still reports that no owner was found
given a page value of 1 or above, when the owner listing is opened, then the listing behaves as it did before this slice
non_goals: The veterinarian directory's handling of a page value below 1: the request names the owner listing only; recorded as an Open Question
A page value past the last page: outside the quoted request; recorded as an Open Question
A page value that is not a whole number, or a whole number too large to read: outside this slice by a reversible decision; recorded as an Open Question
notes: Intake line 1 carries no decisions and quotes 'any page value below 1'. No REQ or Non-Goals row conflicts, so no pushback was raised. Reversible decision: 'any page value below 1' is scoped to whole numbers the listing can read today; a later slice can extend it cheaply. No prd-autofix records exist to audit. docs/ubiquitous-language.md needs no change: the slice introduces no domain term. The bug report also asks for the cause; that belongs to the design and implementation stages and is not recorded here.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Covered by docs/architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row: normalizing a request parameter to its permitted range is binding, not a business rule, so the fix stays in OwnerController (docs/system-design.md § Contracts). No service, new type, or shared helper. Cause, from grep and a read of the source (IntelliJ oracle not connected, the weaker basis): OwnerController.findPaginatedForOwnersLastName passes page - 1 to PageRequest.of, which refuses a negative index, and the exception reaches the error page. Fix: normalize page to at least 1 at the top of processFindForm, before any arithmetic, and use that one value for both the repository query and the pagination model. The only docs edit is REQ-OWN-005 joining the OwnerController Implements cell.
integration_points: Repository boundary (OwnerRepository): framework stub, the existing @MockitoBean in OwnerControllerTests. A hand-written double does not fit because the @WebMvcTest class already wires this bean and the interface inherits the full Spring Data surface. Per docs/testing-principles.md § A stub is a stand-in, stub the first-page request by exact Pageable argument (index 0, the controller's page size), never any(Pageable.class), so the listed owners prove which page was asked for.
Framework transport: MockMvc, the sanctioned harness. docs/testing-principles.md places normalization at the web level, so no unit test of an extracted helper.
Binding: no new entry point. The existing GET /owners handler keeps its scalar int page parameter and Owner search binding under the existing id disallow list.

patterns.description: processFindForm already normalizes lastName inline before the query; page normalization follows the same in-handler shape

risks.risk: Integer.MIN_VALUE: clamping after subtraction fails, because page - 1 wraps to Integer.MAX_VALUE, PageRequest accepts it, and the listing reports not found with no error page. Same for Math.max(page - 1, 0).
risks.mitigation: Clamp the 1-based value before subtracting (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row: normalize to the permitted range at binding). Cover the lowest readable value in theOwnerListingShouldShowTheFirstPageForPageZeroMinusOneAndTheLowestReadableValue, with the stub keyed on the first-page Pageable, since an any(Pageable.class) stub would hide the wrap.

risks.risk: Clamping only inside findPaginatedForOwnersLastName leaves addPaginationModel with the raw value, so currentPage stays below 1, no page is marked current, and the previous and first controls misbehave.
risks.mitigation: Normalize once in processFindForm so both callees receive the same value; assert model attribute currentPage equals 1 (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row).

risks.risk: Scope creep into the non-goals: VetController has the same page - 1 expression, and a non-numeric or too-large page or one past the last page stays unchanged.
risks.mitigation: Leave VetController and those cases alone; the PRD Open Questions hold them (docs/system-design.md § Contracts scopes this id to OwnerController).

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records. Foundational check: no signal trips for this concern. No ADR is cited by the lines touched. Workload: the slice adds no path that scales with data; the change is a constant-time clamp on the existing paged query, so no row is needed. docs/system-design.md has no § Scale and Load section at all, so no row exists to cite for the owner listing; a later slice that adds a data-scaling path must create it. No section was invented here. The repository contract row is unchanged because the repository is not touched.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: PAGE_SIZE = 5 copies the production local `int pageSize = 5;` (OwnerController.java:137) and FIRST_PAGE / PageRequest.of(1, PAGE_SIZE) are built from it. That is hidden coupling the brief names (testing-principles.md, Three-Tier Data Naming: a named value that copies a production constant is coupling). A change of the listing's page size would fail all six new tests while the clamp rule is untouched, so they would fail for a reason other than a defect in the rule.
findings.fix: Stop depending on the size. Stub with a matcher on the page index only, e.g. argThat(pageable -> pageable.getPageNumber() == 0) for the below-one cases and == 1 for the page-2 case, and drop PAGE_SIZE and FIRST_PAGE; the PageImpl in the page-2 test can use the one-arg form with an explicit total only if the template needs it.

recommendations: The two parameterized tests share the same three-row table and the same stub (lines 162-183); they could be one test only if the PRD bullets were merged, so they are left as is. If the table is trimmed, -1 and Integer.MIN_VALUE are the same equivalence class as 0 apart from the explicit edge case 5, which justifies keeping the MIN_VALUE row.
approved_aspects: Placement: the clamp is request-parameter normalization in OwnerController, which docs/system-design.md assigns to the web controller (OwnerController row, REQ-OWN-005 added); testing it through MockMvc at the web layer is correct and no unit-level seam is skipped.

Coverage map (python3 scripts/grading.py coverage-map --feature REQ-OWN-005): 3 Done-when bullets each covered by a test whose name states it (listing opens first page; currentPage 1; multi-match search); edge case 4 covered by theOwnerSearchShouldOpenTheSingleMatchForAPageValueBelowOne and theOwnerSearchShouldReportNotFoundForAPageValueBelowOne; edge case 5 by the Integer.MIN_VALUE row. Declared tests: 6 of 6 present.

The stubs bind the Pageable argument, so the page argument sent is asserted through the observable outcome; removing the clamp makes PageRequest.of(-1, ...) throw, so the tests would fail on that defect. theOwnerListingShouldKeepTheRequestedPageForAPageValueOfOneOrAbove guards against an over-broad clamp.

Parameterized names state every row; each parameterized test holds one assertion set over one equivalence class (below one); no phase comments, no branching, fluent AssertJ/Hamcrest as in the host file.

semantic_surprise.note: Read at OwnerController.java:98 and against lines 110, 124 and 138: Math.max(page, 1) is the identity for page 1 and above and runs before the page - 1 subtraction, so Integer.MIN_VALUE cannot wrap, and the same value feeds both the query and currentPage, so ownersList.html's controls act from page 1.
